unit.summary: Background execution, routing, Foundation correctness, persistence, web trust, device services, and extension boundaries grounded in the active client.

lessons.title: Background execution, notifications, and APNs ownership
lessons.summary: Choose a supported way to finish work after the app leaves the screen. Handle expiration, late results, account changes, and notification delivery as separate outcomes.
objectives: Tell apart an opportunity to run code, notification presentation, and server delivery.
Define what expiration, cancellation, completion, and account changes do to unfinished work.
Follow APNs registration, signed capability requests, payload types, and response handling in the checkout.
Specify physical-device checks without promising a fixed wake-up or delivery time.

sections.title: Ask what can run after the app leaves the screen
sections.html:
Suspension means the process is still present but is not executing its ordinary work. A Swift Task can remain allocated while suspended; that does not let it keep running. iOS can also terminate that process. Think of an Android draft upload and WorkManager refresh, then check iOS’s execution permission separately. Store enough durable information to resume a logical operation and safely handle repeats. A closure holding the only operation ID cannot survive process death.

Foreground, inactive, background, suspended, and terminated describe different circumstances. Inactive can mean a temporary interruption while the app remains visible. Scene activation is separate from application execution: one window becoming inactive does not necessarily mean every window is inactive. Session 034 develops scene ownership; here, ask which application service owns work after its presenting scene disappears. A UI task should usually stop when its owner stops. An account upload may have a longer owner, but needs an approved background mechanism.

Android foreground services and WorkManager provide useful questions about user visibility, constraints, retries, and durable identifiers. They do not map directly to one iOS API. A background mode is not a general exemption from suspension. Apple defines specific allowed use cases, and scheduling is discretionary. Even a correctly submitted request may not run when your product would prefer. Design the UI to show last-known freshness and offer foreground recovery rather than declaring that content will refresh every fifteen minutes.

sections.title: Choose a supported kind of background work
sections.html:
A background lease is finite extra time to finish work already underway. UIApplication.beginBackgroundTask requests one and returns an identifier you must end. It is not a durable job identifier. The request may return .invalid. Install an expiration handler that stops work promptly. End the lease when work finishes successfully too. Other mechanisms, including scheduled BGTask work and background URLSession transfers, have different setup, lifetime, and completion rules. Choose the mechanism from the actual operation.

BGAppRefreshTask and BGProcessingTask, available from iOS 13, are different scheduled opportunities. Register supported identifiers early in application launch, declare permitted identifiers and relevant capabilities, then submit a matching request. earliestBeginDate is a lower-bound preference, not an appointment with the scheduler. Processing constraints such as network or external power influence eligibility, not a completion guarantee. Catch submission errors and maintain foreground fallback.

A background-configured URLSession is appropriate for supported upload and download transfers whose ownership moves beyond an ordinary in-process data request. Use stable session identifiers, file-backed uploads where required, delegate reconnection, and the system's completion handoff. A successful async data(for:) example from session 018 does not establish background-transfer support. File staging, retries, authentication, and server idempotency remain your responsibility.

Apple documents BGContinuedProcessingTask and its request from iOS/iPadOS 26 for work that starts in the foreground and continues with visible progress and user cancellation. The system can still terminate it under resource pressure. Compile against a supporting SDK and use if #available(iOS 26.0, *) with an honest older-OS path. Treat this as an adjacent option, not a replacement already used here. Searches of active Projects Swift sources found finite UIKit leases, but no direct BGTaskScheduler registration. The checked app manifest has an iOS 17 minimum; SDK documentation availability does not raise that deployment minimum or prove a newer path is enabled.

sections.title: Report one outcome and reject late writes
sections.html:
A terminal outcome is the final result reported for an operation. Expiration, success, failure, cancellation, logout, and process death have different meanings. At expiration, request cancellation, close the right to commit, and satisfy the framework’s completion rule. Cancellation is cooperative: ignored requests can still produce a result. Check cancellation and current ownership immediately before committing. Canceling a local upload waiter cannot undo a server write. Reconcile that effect using the operation’s replay-safe server contract.

This standalone Swift state machine models one terminal decision. It does not itself register a background task or stop networking:

enum WorkTerminal: Equatable, Sendable {
    case success, failure, expired, canceled
}
@MainActor
final class WorkFinishGate {
    private var terminal: WorkTerminal?
    private let report: (WorkTerminal) -> Void

    init(report: @escaping (WorkTerminal) -> Void) {
        self.report = report
    }

    func finish(_ outcome: WorkTerminal) {
        guard terminal == nil else { return }
        terminal = outcome
        report(outcome)
    }
}

The enum gives completion outcomes explicit names. @MainActor isolates access to the optional terminal state. It does not create a thread dedicated to this gate. @escaping allows the callback to outlive initialization. guard ignores a second finish attempt. Storing the winning state before report also blocks a reentrant callback from reporting twice. Every caller must use this isolation domain for the rule to hold. A Boolean read and written on unrelated delegate queues does not provide the same protection.

Adapt the winning outcome to the API in use: end a UIKit lease, or call a BGTask's setTaskCompleted(success:), or supply the fetch result. These callbacks have different types and meanings. Ending a lease does not automatically cancel a Task. A production adapter retains its task handle, invalidates commit ownership, and invokes the appropriate terminal callback once.

A worked synchronous gate check records outcomes in a local array: finish success, then finish expired, then finish failure; expect exactly [.success]. A fresh gate receives expired first and then success; expect exactly [.expired]. Run both calls within MainActor. Pair the gate with RefreshCommit in the exercise: close the commit owner before releasing a delayed success, assert commit rejects, and then assert one expired completion. Reporting count and durable acceptance are separate invariants; testing one does not establish the other.

sections.title: Keep push registration separate from alert permission
sections.html:
APNs is Apple’s remote-notification transport. The app registers with UIApplication and gets a device token in a delegate callback. Alert authorization is a separate request to UNUserNotificationCenter. A person can deny banners while registration or other app state still exists. A server token record does not prove that a banner may be shown. Settings can change outside the app, so reread the relevant presentation settings when it becomes active. Then check the signed environment and server binding.

A token is opaque binary data tied to an app/device/environment relationship, not a permanent user identifier. Register the current token with the appropriate server account, handle registration failure, and update bindings after account transitions. Do not assume token byte length or print the full token for diagnostics. The checkout forwards Data from AppDelegate and constructs a hexadecimal representation in Application. Inspect that actual path rather than copying an older description-based conversion as a general encoding recipe.

The APNs environment entitlement is signed into the application. Provider requests must use the matching APNs environment and topic, normally the app's bundle identifier. Source files named Prod or QA do not prove the final value: the inspected ZocdocProd.entitlements contains aps-environment = development. This is a source fact, not a diagnosis that production delivery is broken. Inspect the signed archive, provisioning/export path, server topic, and endpoint before making an operational claim.

Keep provider credentials on the service, never in the mobile bundle. APNs acceptance establishes that a request was accepted for processing; it is not proof that a person saw it. Invalid or obsolete tokens, wrong topic, mismatched environment, and transient provider failures need separate handling and synthetic diagnostics that exclude sensitive payloads.

sections.title: Separate delivery, presentation, and a person’s action
sections.html:
A notification lifecycle is the sequence from scheduling or sending through presentation and response. Alert pushes, background-only pushes, and local notifications follow different paths. A background APNs update uses aps.content-available and matching push headers. Its low-priority delivery is discretionary: it can be delayed, throttled, or discarded. It cannot be a precise alarm or proof that a transaction finished. Reconcile authoritative data when the app next runs, including when force-quit prevented expected background work.

UNUserNotificationCenterDelegate.willPresent decides presentation while the app is foregrounded. The notification-response callback handles a person's tap or category action. It is not called simply because a remote notification reached the device. Distinguish default open, dismiss, and custom action identifiers. Register categories before scheduling notifications that reference them, and keep payload parsing bounded. Unknown identifiers should produce a safe outcome, not an unconditional mutation.

The active Application sets foreground presentation to list and banner and routes medication reminder responses before its marketing path. That teaches a concrete privacy and ownership seam. Completion follows the local response handling; a route requiring authentication is handled separately. An action can be delivered after its original data has changed, so pass an occurrence identifier and validate current state rather than recomputing the target from the wall clock.

The Notifications extension subclasses Braze's service extension. A notification service extension can modify eligible remote alert content within a bounded lifetime; it is not a general application background worker. Its fallback and time-expiration behavior matter. A source subclass establishes integration, not proof that all provider payloads invoke it or that attachments always arrive.

sections.title: Write rules for cancellation, retry, and locked data
sections.html:
An operation policy states who owns work and which outcomes are allowed. Name the durable input, owner, eligibility, effort limit, success rule, retry categories, and recovery trigger. Offline data may wait for another opportunity. An unauthorized response needs a different decision. Expiration must not become empty successful data. Keep enough non-sensitive metadata to distinguish these cases. Then check account ownership and protected-data access at the actual commit point, not only at the screen that started the work.

An epoch is a changing ownership number, not an account name. Capture it before waiting for remote work. Validate it where the final write is serialized, including if account A changes to B and later back to A. Lesson 020 guards memory-cache updates this way. A later disk write on another queue needs an equivalent check in its own owner. Canceling the screen’s waiter cannot guarantee that an SDK callback or background transfer will not refill an old account’s files.

Locked-device behavior also affects execution. A permitted background wake does not guarantee readable Keychain items or files. An unavailable protected item is not necessarily deleted or corrupt. Preserve its error, avoid replacing it with an empty store, and retry through a defined recovery path. Select protection classes from actual access requirements; do not weaken them merely because a callback sometimes arrives while locked.

Keep retries bounded and idempotent. The background scheduler is not your exact retry clock. A local notification's requested date is also not a medical or delivery guarantee. The learning exercises use synthetic refreshes and reminder-like identifiers only; specialist notification, clinical, security, and release review remains necessary for a real high-stakes feature.

sections.title: Separate source checks from device checks
sections.html:
Evidence is an observation that supports a specific claim. Read the finite lease in AppDelegate, remote-notification handling in Application, medication response branch, and source entitlements together. Record who receives work, completes it, and changes account state. A comment promising one completion is intent. Its isolation and fallback paths still need inspection. A source capability request likewise does not establish what the installed signed artifact contains. Keep those layers separate in the verification table.

Build a device matrix that separates foreground delivery, background delivery, cold launch from a tap, Settings changes, network failure, locked protected data, and a duplicate or late action. Observe terminal callback counts and durable state, rather than accepting a banner screenshot as evidence of correct processing. Verify scheduled notification contents with synthetic fixtures; never copy a real payload into course notes.

For a scheduler experiment, record OS, device, build, request submission, eventual invocation if observed, expiration, and resulting freshness. “Not invoked during this observation window” is valid evidence and must not be converted into a scheduling defect without more information. For APNs, add environment/topic evidence and provider outcome. Simulator tests of parsing and completion cannot validate signed-device delivery or actual energy budgets.

Your handoff should say which invariants were practiced and which operating-system paths remain unverified. This lesson provides execution and ownership reasoning; it does not claim a full BGTask migration, background URLSession implementation, or successful production push test.

quiz.question: earliestBeginDate is tomorrow at 09:00. What can the product promise?
options: The task runs exactly at 09:00.
It is a scheduling preference; refresh may occur later or not in the observed window.
It runs at 09:00 if a Swift actor owns it.
quiz.explanation: Eligibility is discretionary. An actor controls local state access, not the operating system's scheduling policy. Show freshness and retain foreground recovery.

quiz.question: A source file named ZocdocProd.entitlements contains development. Which conclusion is supported?
options: All installed production pushes are broken.
The server should send to both environments blindly.
The source requests development; verify the signed/exported artifact and provider configuration.
quiz.explanation: File names are not signed evidence. Source, provisioning, export, installed identity, topic, and provider endpoint must be traced before diagnosing delivery.

quiz.question: The expiration handler cancels a task that later returns success. What still protects account data?
options: A commit guard for cancellation and current ownership plus one terminal transition.
Returning an empty collection.
Increasing the scheduler priority.
quiz.explanation: Cancellation is cooperative. The final serialized store commit must reject expired or superseded work, and framework completion must not run twice.

exercise.brief: Build a fake refresh lease and a table of verification evidence. Control success, expiration, late results, and logout without registering pushes or editing client settings.
steps: Use WorkFinishGate with a fake completion recorder and a Task handle kept by the owner.
Give the store an account epoch and a may-commit flag. Keep validation and replacement in one serialized operation.
Hold a fake response, expire the lease, then release that response even if it ignored cancellation.
Repeat for success, failure, repeated finish calls, and an A-to-B-to-A account transition.
List the APNs artifact checks separately and mark physical-device delivery pending.
acceptance: Exactly one terminal completion is recorded per fake lease.
Expiration cancels work and prevents a later response from replacing the snapshot.
Changing account ownership blocks old writes even if the account text becomes A again.
The ledger distinguishes source entitlements from signed archive evidence.
No timing, APNs delivery, or background-transfer verification is claimed from the fake.
exercise.solution:
The scratch adapter needs two rules: report a terminal outcome once, and accept a durable update only from its current owner. Keep both decisions on MainActor for this experiment. Do not place an await between the ownership check and snapshot replacement. Use controlled fake gates from lesson 020 to choose which event arrives first. RefreshCommit below models only this acceptance boundary. It neither writes a database nor registers background work. Real disk commits need the same check inside their actual transaction owner.

@MainActor
final class RefreshCommit {
    private var epoch = 0
    private var accepting = true
    private(set) var snapshot: [String] = []

    func ticket() -> Int { epoch }

    func close() {
        accepting = false
        epoch += 1
    }

    func startNewOwner() {
        epoch += 1
        accepting = true
        snapshot = []
    }

    func commit(_ values: [String], ticket: Int) -> Bool {
        guard accepting, ticket == epoch else { return false }
        snapshot = values
        return true
    }
}

Capture ticket() before awaiting the fake remote. On expiration call close(), cancel the retained task, and finish the gate as expired. When the fake is released, check Task cancellation, then call commit with the original ticket; it must fail even if the fake ignored cancellation. Normal success commits first and reports success only after that succeeds. Ordinary failure preserves the previous snapshot and reports failure. A second terminal call has no effect.

private(set) lets the harness inspect the snapshot but keeps mutation inside the owner. Incrementing epoch invalidates all prior tickets. Starting another owner increments it again, so textual account equality cannot restore validity. The methods are synchronous; a disk adapter would need to perform the same validation in its actual transaction owner, not validate here and later await an unguarded file write.

The worked ledger records the fake's completion sequence, snapshot before and after each case, and pending device rows. The APNs row requests the installed bundle ID, signed aps environment, compatible profile/export path, provider endpoint and topic, current token binding, payload push type, and observed response. A foreground banner screenshot answers only presentation. No exact scheduler cadence or clinical reminder reliability follows from this exercise.

simple.story: Ravi borrows a room to sort parcels. The caretaker can ask him to leave when the room is needed. Ravi writes down the unfinished parcel numbers so he can resume later. When asked to leave, he stops accepting new sorted piles and hands back the key once. A helper may still bring a pile prepared earlier. Ravi checks whether that job is still open before accepting it. A promise that the room might be free tomorrow is not a booking for nine o’clock.
simple.meaning: Background execution is a limited opportunity controlled by the system. Cancellation asks work to stop. The final owner must still reject late results after expiration or an account change, and report completion once.

example.before: A fake refresh owns epoch 7, may commit, and shows the old snapshot. Its response is held by a test gate.
example.change: Expire the lease first: close commit ownership, cancel the task, and report expired. Then release the held response.
example.after: The late response cannot replace the snapshot. The completion recorder contains one expired outcome even if success is attempted afterward.

lessons.title: Universal links, routes, authentication gates, and App Clips
lessons.summary: Turn an incoming link into a small checked route. Wait for the right scene and account, then keep late login results from opening an old destination.
objectives: Tell apart URL delivery, website association, route parsing, and permission to read a resource.
Parse URLs into small route values with explicit limits for encoding and repeated query fields.
Own the pending route through startup, canceled login, newer links, and account changes.
Trace the App Clip’s separate invocation path and list the service and distribution checks still needed.

sections.title: Treat a link as a request
sections.html:
A route is a checked value naming a requested destination. Before producing one, distinguish link delivery from permission to use it. Android Intent filters select possible receivers; the receiving activity still parses input and checks login. On iOS, a custom scheme advertises an entry point but does not prove website ownership. Universal links use HTTPS and a domain-to-app association. Neither authorizes access to card alpha. The service must still decide whether the current account may read that card.

Draw four boundaries: operating-system delivery, syntactic parsing, account/feature gating, and destination execution. A parser should produce a small route value or an explicit rejection. It should not present controllers, access Keychain, request permissions, or issue a booking. This lets parser fixtures stay deterministic and avoids side effects while inspecting a malformed link. A coordinator resolves the route only when its scene and account dependencies are ready.

The Android analogy breaks at callback and lifecycle details. Intent extras, Android verified App Links, iOS browsing activities, and custom scheme callbacks have different delivery and verification rules. Do not expect a single equivalent of onNewIntent to cover every cold and warm launch. A routing framework is useful only after you know which inputs it receives and when. Test the entry adapters and the pure parser separately.

Use synthetic identifiers in exercises. A route category can be diagnostic metadata; the raw URL may include credentials or private information. A familiar host is not permission to export its complete query string.

sections.title: Check both the app and the website
sections.html:
Association is the agreement that makes certain website links eligible to open an app. The app requests an Associated Domains entry such as applinks:learn.example.com. The website serves apple-app-site-association, a JSON file without a filename extension, normally under /.well-known/. It uses HTTPS with a valid certificate and no redirect. Its identifiers combine the application identifier prefix and bundle ID. Check the actual prefix before substituting a team ID. Both sides need verification.

Path and query matching in the association file decide which web links are eligible for app handling. Ordered exclusions and specific rules matter. The app's parser must still reject unsupported or malformed input. Association is not a substitute for validation, and webcredentials: is a different associated-domain service from applinks:. Declaring one does not grant the other. App Clip association uses its own service entry and identifiers.

On supported OS versions, Apple’s associated-domain CDN caches the website association. Updating the server file may not update a device’s state immediately. Record the installed build, server response, and observed opening behavior without promising a cache-refresh time. Opening context matters too. Typing in a browser address bar, following a same-site link, and tapping from another app can behave differently. A person’s opening preference can also affect the result. Test the context that the product actually needs.

The checkout declares several concrete domains in Prod and QA source entitlements. That establishes requested support, not the currently deployed AASA contents, CDN response, signed entitlements, or every possible launch context. This lesson does not fetch company association files or validate their production ownership.

sections.title: Parse into a small value with clear limits
sections.html:
A parser turns raw input into a checked value or a rejection. This Foundation-only parser accepts one synthetic HTTPS path shape. It rejects all queries and fragments so extra or repeated fields cannot gain accidental meaning. If a real route needs query fields, first define allowed keys, how often each may occur, length, encoding, and missing versus empty values. The parser should not open a screen, read credentials, or make a network request while checking the input.

import Foundation

enum LessonRoute: Equatable, Sendable {
    case card(String)
}
enum RouteError: Error { case unsupported }

func parseLessonRoute(_ url: URL) throws -> LessonRoute {
    guard let parts = URLComponents(
        url: url, resolvingAgainstBaseURL: false
    ), parts.scheme?.lowercased() == "https",
       parts.host?.lowercased() == "learn.example.com",
       parts.user == nil, parts.password == nil,
       parts.port == nil,
       parts.query == nil, parts.fragment == nil else {
        throw RouteError.unsupported
    }
    let segments = parts.percentEncodedPath.split(
        separator: "/", omittingEmptySubsequences: false
    )
    guard segments.count == 3,
          segments[0].isEmpty, segments[1] == "cards",
          !segments[2].isEmpty else {
        throw RouteError.unsupported
    }
    let id = String(segments[2])
    let allowed = CharacterSet(
        charactersIn: "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789-"
    )
    guard id.utf8.count <= 40,
          id.unicodeScalars.allSatisfy({ allowed.contains($0) }) else {
        throw RouteError.unsupported
    }
    return .card(id)
}

guard let unwraps components and combines rejection conditions. Optional chaining accesses scheme or host only if present. The parser compares an exact normalized host, so learn.example.com.evil.invalid fails. Reading percentEncodedPath and allowing only literal ASCII avoids accepting encoded slashes or double-decoded identifiers. Empty subsequences remain visible, making double slashes and trailing slashes reject rather than silently normalize.

utf8.count is a byte bound; unicodeScalars checks the allowlist. Here the accepted alphabet is ASCII, so that bound also has an uncomplicated character interpretation. The enum stores a validated ID. This parser is stricter than the real product parser and is not a proposed replacement for all existing links.

sections.title: Keep a pending route until its scene is ready
sections.html:
A pending route is a checked destination waiting for the UI and account to become ready. Universal links arrive as browsing NSUserActivity values with a possible webpageURL. Custom schemes use URL-opening callbacks. In scene-based apps, cold launch can put input in connection options; warm input can arrive later through scene callbacks. App-delegate lifecycles use other paths. Read the target’s actual declarations before wiring adapters. Implementing every possible callback without a policy can deliver the same navigation twice.

The active AppLaunchRouter forwards already-unwrapped delegate-shaped inputs to existing Application behavior. Its comments explicitly describe a seam for a future scene cutover. That is a verified adapter, not evidence that the main app has already completed the cutover. The App Clip, separately, has a SceneDelegate that handles both connection-option activities and later continuations. Keep these target facts distinct.

A coordinator may receive a route before the root UI exists. Retain a bounded pending destination, with an explicit policy for later arrivals: latest wins, queue with a cap, or reject while handling. Do not accumulate an unbounded list of external URLs. Clear a pending destination when consumed, canceled, expired by product policy, or invalidated by account ownership. Assigning a view controller after awaiting startup is a commit that still needs a scene identity check.

Choose which scene should receive the route on a multiple-window device. Reusing a global presenter without checking its scene can put login in the wrong window. Persist restoration state only when it is suitable for later replay; do not persist a one-time authorization code as ordinary navigation state.

sections.title: After login, check the route’s current owner
sections.html:
Authentication establishes a session. Authorization decides whether that session may access the requested resource. For a synthetic account-only card, parse the route, check feature availability, and retain the checked value while presenting login. After success, resolve the current account and request the resource. Login cancellation is an expected outcome. Clear or retain the pending route according to a written rule. It must not claim navigation succeeded or create a loop that repeatedly asks the person to sign in.

Route and account ownership answer different questions: which destination is current, and which login period may apply the result? If another route arrives or the account changes while work waits, the earlier completion must not replace the current destination. Use an epoch for A-to-B-to-A; matching the text A again cannot restore the old ticket. Check ownership after each relevant suspension. The service can still deny that card even when the local account and route remain current.

Links that embed an authentication callback require protocol-specific validation: exact redirect shape, state bound to the request, and PKCE where required. A normal route parser should not accept arbitrary “redirect” parameters and forward credentials to their targets. Keep callback handling inside the authentication owner. Do not equate Universal Link association with OAuth state validation or service authorization.

For destructive actions, navigation can show a review screen, but an incoming link must not silently perform the action under the current session. Replayed links, notification taps after logout, and stale widget URLs all reach the same trust boundary. Session 054 adds the browser and system authentication lifetime details.

sections.title: Treat an App Clip as its own product
sections.html:
An App Clip is a separately built small experience associated with a full app. Its invocation is the request that starts it, including a URL for a useful small task. Associated domains and configured App Clip experiences help discovery. An appclips: source entry alone does not create a working distributed experience. Apple account setup, signed artifacts, and the supported invocation context need separate checks. The clip also has its own process, dependencies, resources, and lifecycle.

The inspected app manifest declares a ZocdocAppClip target with iOS 17 deployment, sources, resources, and its own entitlements. Its SceneDelegate extracts a webpage URL, parses an AppClipLink, chooses intake, practice, professional, or default UI, and retains navigation coordinators. This is concrete checkout support. It does not mean the full application's route parser, session, containers, or features are automatically available in the clip process.

For cold invocation, the clip drains connection-option user activities into the same continuation method. The retained coordinator is essential because otherwise a temporary coordinator can disappear before navigation completes. Inspect references and errors just as you would an Android dynamic experience. Swift's ARC terminology differs from tracing garbage collection: keeping a reference establishes ownership, not just a vague “prevent garbage collection” convention.

Limit dependencies to the clip's task and design a useful web or full-app fallback. App Clip size limits and eligible APIs vary with OS and distribution rules; check current official guidance for the exact release instead of embedding a universal numerical limit in this course. Installation, credential handoff, invocation validation, and special capabilities deserve a dedicated specialist lab.

sections.title: Test parsing and link delivery separately
sections.html:
A parser fixture is controlled input used to check a local parsing rule. It can show that the synthetic host and valid ID produce a route. It cannot show that iOS delivers that URL to the app. A simulator command may inject a URL directly and bypass parts of association and installation. A browser fallback and a signed-device cross-app tap check other layers. Label each observation with the layer it covers before claiming universal-link support works.

Include fixtures for a deceptive suffix host, HTTP instead of HTTPS, embedded user/password, unexpected port, unknown query, duplicate query, encoded slash, empty ID, excessive length, trailing path, and mixed case where allowed. Add cold start, warm start, UI-not-ready, logged-out login, canceled login, foreign-resource rejection, second route during login, and account switch during loading. Assert destination count as well as destination content.

The checkout parser explicitly rejects unknown trailing medication-reminder segments. Application also validates accepted HTTP domains before parsing and carries separate external-fallback behavior. Trace both decisions; a parser accepting a URL does not mean Application will open it internally. Conversely, an external fallback may be intentional rather than a parse failure hidden from the person.

Your evidence ledger should name source anchors, fixture results, and pending AASA/device/distribution checks. No part of this synthetic exercise verifies live company links or claims that an App Clip invocation has been distributed successfully.

quiz.question: AASA associates a trusted domain with the app. Does that authorize the card ID in a link?
options: Yes, the OS has authenticated the card owner.
No; parsing, account gates, and service authorization remain necessary.
Only if the URL has no query.
quiz.explanation: Association establishes a domain/app relationship and eligible link handling. It does not authorize user-supplied resource identifiers.

quiz.question: Why does the synthetic parser keep empty path components?
options: To silently normalize double slashes.
To make malformed path shapes reject explicitly.
To support any number of trailing segments.
quiz.explanation: Keeping empty subsequences makes a double slash or trailing slash visible. The route contract accepts exactly the intended path shape.

exercise.solution:
Keep the parser pure and put pending-route decisions in a small MainActor owner. Choose latest-wins explicitly: accepting beta replaces pending alpha. Every new route changes the ticket, even if its value equals the earlier route. Account reset and cancellation invalidate it too. accept returns the ticket to capture before waiting for login. consume checks and clears synchronously. The code below models that one decision. The scene and service must still authorize the actual navigation.

@MainActor
final class PendingLessonRoute {
    private var generation = 0
    private var pending: LessonRoute?

    func accept(_ route: LessonRoute) -> Int {
        generation += 1
        pending = route
        return generation
    }

    func invalidate() {
        generation += 1
        pending = nil
    }

    func consume(ticket: Int) -> LessonRoute? {
        guard ticket == generation, let route = pending else {
            return nil
        }
        pending = nil
        return route
    }
}

accept returns the ticket captured before login. consume both validates and clears synchronously; repeating it returns nil. Invalidate on account changes and cancellation, then check the scene still owns presentation before navigation. A production implementation also resolves current service authorization, handles feature flags, and defines user feedback when a route cannot be completed.

For a worked ordering, accept card alpha, pause login, accept card beta, then complete alpha's login. Consuming alpha's ticket returns nil. Complete the current login and consume beta's ticket once. Repeat with account invalidation and A-to-B-to-A; neither should recover alpha's original ticket. Avoid sleeps: explicitly gate fake completion and assert both the count and selected destination.

The association ledger requests the signed app identifier and associated-domains entries, website JSON and HTTPS response without redirects, eligible path rules, current installed build, actual cross-app tap behavior, browser fallback, and App Clip experience configuration. lessons.title: Foundation correctness: civil time, Unicode, locale, and files
lessons.summary: Choose what a date, text range, number, or file means before choosing an API. Make time zones, text boundaries, locale rules, and storage failures explicit.
objectives: Tell apart an instant, a calendar date, a daily local time, a time zone, and elapsed duration.
Choose daylight-saving and locale rules and check them with named fixtures.
Convert Swift text and UTF-16 ranges without treating bytes, code units, and characters as the same thing.
Choose storage directories, replacement rules, backup, protection, and failure outcomes for the data.

sections.title: Choose an instant, a date, or a local clock time
sections.html:
An instant is one point on the timeline. Foundation Date represents an instant; it stores no time zone, locale, or calendar. Your Android Instant, LocalDate, LocalTime, ZonedDateTime, and Duration experience helps separate these meanings. Two displays of one Date can show different local days. A birthday chosen as year, month, and day is usually a civil date. It should not silently become midnight in whichever time zone later formats it. Choose the product meaning first.

DateComponents stores selected calendar fields. Calendar interprets those fields and performs calendar arithmetic. TimeZone supplies civil-time offset rules, and Locale supplies conventions for presentation. These are separate inputs. A numeric offset such as minus five hours describes one offset; a region identifier such as America/New_York describes rules that can change with daylight saving and historical transitions. Storing only an offset loses those rules.

Ask what the product means before choosing fields. An appointment with a service-defined instant and venue zone is different from “daily at 09:00 wherever the person is.” A floating reminder may store hour and minute plus a travel policy. An annual civil birthday stores civil components. A stopwatch needs elapsed duration. Converting all four to Date simplifies a database column while moving ambiguity into every caller.

The checkout has a concrete example: MedicationRemindersCalendar explicitly uses the device system zone because Application's default zone override differs from the widget process and SwiftUI date picker. Do not assume Calendar.current has the same meaning across processes. Use an injected calendar and named policy.

sections.title: Choose rules for skipped and repeated local times
sections.html:
Civil time is a local calendar date and clock time. Adding 86,400 seconds advances an instant by a fixed duration. Moving one day with Calendar advances calendar meaning; around daylight-saving changes the elapsed duration can differ. A local day can be shorter or longer than twenty-four hours. Some local times never occur and others occur twice. Even midnight is not every historical day’s boundary. Use startOfDay(for:) for the calendar boundary, then choose an explicit gap and repeated-time policy.

Some local times do not occur during a spring-forward gap. Other local times occur twice during a fall-back transition. Calendar.nextDate offers matching and repeated-time policies; choose them from the business requirement. Strict matching can skip a non-existent candidate, while other policies adjust it. The word “daily” does not settle whether to skip, advance, or preserve smaller components. A medication workflow needs specialist policy; use ordinary synthetic reminders for this lab.

import Foundation

func nextSyntheticNine(after instant: Date, zone: TimeZone) -> Date? {
    var calendar = Calendar(identifier: .gregorian)
    calendar.timeZone = zone
    return calendar.nextDate(
        after: instant,
        matching: DateComponents(hour: 9, minute: 0, second: 0),
        matchingPolicy: .nextTime,
        repeatedTimePolicy: .first,
        direction: .forward
    )
}

var permits changing the calendar value; let would prevent assigning its timezone. Argument labels make the policy visible. The optional return requires handling a failure to find a result. This example chooses the first repeated match and next-time adjustment; it does not assert that those policies fit every reminder. Test a missing 02:30 and a repeated 01:30 separately, not only the uncomplicated 09:00 example.

Timezone databases and political rules can change. Persist the semantic inputs, and record the timezone/OS context of fixtures. A future scheduled civil time is not necessarily a permanently settled UTC instant.

sections.title: Use different clocks for timestamps and elapsed time
sections.html:
A wall clock supplies dates and times that can be saved or compared with a service timestamp. A monotonic clock measures elapsed duration without following wall-time jumps. Use Date for persisted instants. Use a clock such as ContinuousClock for elapsed timing inside the process. Subtracting two Date values is not a reliable timeout rule if system time changes. Do not save a process clock instant as though it were a portable server timestamp. Parsing and display each need their own rules too.

For a wire timestamp, define an exact format contract: offset or UTC marker, fractional seconds, allowed precision, and failure behavior. ISO8601DateFormatter or Date's ISO8601 format style can express supported representations, but one configuration does not accept every string that resembles ISO 8601. Test fractional and non-fractional fixtures and reject malformed values. A timestamp without an offset needs an explicitly named interpretation rather than a guess based on the device zone.

For localized display, prefer semantic format styles or localized templates. Literal yyyy is calendar year; YYYY is week-based year and can differ near a year boundary. Quoting a literal Z in a format does not convert an instant to UTC. The formatter's timezone must also be set. Locale, calendar, and zone belong in fixture setup, not in a presumed ambient global.

The active DateFormatter helper caches by format, zone, and locale and also contains a thread-dictionary legacy path. Read how callers configure these shared reference objects. Do not mutate a cached formatter's settings casually, and do not treat thread-local storage as task-local isolation: a Swift task can resume on a different thread.

sections.title: Separate display conventions from arithmetic
sections.html:
A locale supplies conventions such as decimal separators, grouping marks, and date order. The text 1,234 can have different meanings under different conventions. Decide whether an input follows the visible locale or a fixed machine grammar. NumberFormatter or a parse strategy can help, but test leniency and whether the whole input is accepted. Deleting punctuation and guessing is unsafe. Separately choose exact monetary representation, scale, and rounding; formatted text cannot define the amount’s arithmetic.

Represent exact money according to the service contract, often integer minor units with a currency code or Decimal with a specified scale and rounding rule. Double is a binary floating-point value; many decimal fractions cannot be represented exactly. Decimal is not a substitute for deciding rounding, currency scale, overflow, and business rules. A formatter presents a value; it does not authorize a charge or establish the arithmetic contract.

Localized number styles can produce non-Latin digits and non-breaking separators. A user's locale can change while a feature remains active. Tests fixed to en_US make string equality deterministic, but they must be paired with product-policy tests for other locales. Keep transport encoding independent of display output: a localized formatted amount should not become the JSON number or query representation.

The same distinction appears in language. Translating a month label is not choosing the appointment zone. Choosing a timezone is not choosing a calendar. Session 022 covers translation resources and reading direction; this section adds correctness at the data boundary. A review should name all three inputs, including when they deliberately differ.

sections.title: Count the kind of text unit the boundary needs
sections.html:
A Unicode code unit is an encoding unit, not necessarily a displayed character. Java and Kotlin String indexing commonly uses UTF-16 units. Swift String instead presents Characters, each an extended grapheme cluster. One family emoji may contain several scalars and many bytes. An accented letter can have composed or decomposed representation. Character count, scalar count, UTF-16 length, and byte count therefore answer different questions. Choose the unit before making a text limit or selection range.

let composed = "é"
let decomposed = "e\u{301}"
let sameText = composed == decomposed
let characterCount = decomposed.count
let wireBytes = decomposed.utf8.count

let text = "A👩🏽‍💻B"
let range = text.range(of: "B")!
let foundationRange = NSRange(range, in: text)
let recovered = Range(foundationRange, in: text)

These known literals justify the example’s forced range unwrap; real lookup must handle no match. Swift equality respects canonical equivalence, but equal text need not have equal wire bytes. At Foundation text boundaries, NSRange generally uses UTF-16 offsets. Convert using the actual String and convert back with Range(_:in:), which can reject an invalid range. A successful conversion may still end inside one displayed Character. For character-based editing, separately check both endpoints against actual grapheme boundaries.

For character-based selection, this Foundation helper checks both endpoints against the String's actual Character boundaries:

func isCharacterAligned(_ nsRange: NSRange, in text: String) -> Bool {
    guard let range = Range(nsRange, in: text) else { return false }
    let boundaries = Set(text.indices).union([text.endIndex])
    return boundaries.contains(range.lowerBound)
        && boundaries.contains(range.upperBound)
}

Including endIndex permits a selection ending at the end of the text. Building this Set scans the string; reuse a suitable boundary policy for repeated editing checks rather than assuming constant cost.

Do not manufacture a Swift String.Index from an integer byte offset or reuse indices after mutating the string. Repeatedly walking from startIndex can also create quadratic work; scan once or use an appropriate view. Bound both user-visible length and wire-byte size when the endpoint imposes both. Unicode normalization, case folding, confusable identifiers, and collation need a service-aligned security policy; lowercasing display names is not such a policy.

sections.title: Choose a directory that fits the file’s purpose
sections.html:
A sandbox is the app’s allowed filesystem container. It does not make every directory suitable for every file. Documents holds user-facing durable material under the product’s document rules. Application Support holds app-managed durable data. Caches holds replaceable content that the system may remove. Temporary storage holds short-lived material. An irreplaceable draft cannot have its only copy in Caches. Choose durability and visibility first, then use FileManager and file-URL APIs to construct the path.

Obtain directories from FileManager and build paths with URL file APIs. URL(fileURLWithPath:) interprets a filesystem path; URL(string:) parses a URL string and is not a general substitute. Create required parent directories and handle errors. Treat a user-supplied filename as untrusted: reject path traversal and inappropriate separators or generate an internal opaque name. Sandboxing does not excuse overwriting another file inside your own container.

Atomic replacement helps avoid exposing a partially written file. It does not serialize a read-modify-write sequence across tasks or processes. Two writers can both load the same snapshot and atomically replace it, losing one update. Backups and protected-data availability are separate policies. Set them deliberately and verify the resulting resource attributes on supported devices.

For document-provider URLs outside your normal container, security-scoped access and coordinated file access may be necessary. Balance start/stop access and copy or bookmark only under a defined lifetime. This is an adjacent document-integration topic; a synthetic sandbox exercise does not establish provider interoperability.

sections.title: Keep missing, locked, corrupt, and failed writes distinct
sections.html:
A storage error category tells the caller what went wrong and how it might recover. A missing file differs from an unreadable protected file, bad schema, full storage, or failed replacement. The generic File helper returns Bool or nil and collapses several causes. That may suit an optional cache, but not every durable store. The newer medication store throws corruptData separately and injects its clock. Read each adapter’s actual behavior before adopting its failure contract.

File protection controls when protected bytes can be accessed. completeUnlessOpen allows continued access through a file already opened while unlocked. It does not allow any closed protected file to be reopened after lock. That is different from after-first-unlock availability. A background wake must still handle unreadable data. Source comments can describe the intended use, but the retained handle and a physical-device check establish whether the real path can read in that state.

The store writes atomically and then applies protection and backup exclusion. A review should examine creation/replacement attributes and failure between these steps, rather than declare all writes transactionally protected because each API appears in the file. No vulnerability or runtime result is asserted here. Select a storage adapter whose failure semantics fit the data's sensitivity and durability.

Keychain remains the appropriate separate facility for small credentials under a chosen access policy. File protection is not application-level authorization, and an App Group expands the set of entitled processes that can access a shared container. Account epochs and scoped cleanup remain necessary even when every byte is encrypted at rest.

sections.title: Make a table of meaning and expected results
sections.html:
A fixture is controlled data with a stated expected outcome. Use separate rows for one instant shown in two zones, a birthday unaffected by travel, a short DST day, a repeated local hour, and a device-zone reminder. Add composed and decomposed text, emoji ranges, and decimal input in two locales. Assert the meaning or numeric value first. Check display separately: OS locale data can change exact wording even when the underlying instant is still correct.

The checkout's reminder calendar addresses a real cross-process zone discrepancy, so compare app and widget policy explicitly. The date formatter's template cache listens for locale changes; that is useful source evidence, not proof that every cached formatter or visible label updates correctly. Include a runtime locale or zone change in an eventual device test.

For files, use a unique synthetic temporary directory and test missing versus corrupt content, failed save, and atomic visibility. Locked protection and backup behavior require an iOS device and actual container attributes. Avoid deleting production stores as a troubleshooting exercise. Record which cases you executed and which remain planned.

These exercises cover everyday Foundation correctness. Full internationalization, calendar-domain policy, Unicode security, coordinated document editing, and unsafe byte manipulation remain specialist work; they are not completed by recognizing the relevant API names.

exercise.solution:
The worked time fixture names the calendar and time zone rather than using changing device defaults. It constructs New York noon on 9 March 2024 and advances one calendar day. The expected local result is noon on 10 March; the expected duration is 82,800 seconds. Those assertions check different meanings. The Foundation code throws if constructing or advancing the fixture fails. Substituting the current Date would hide that failure and make the test’s inputs meaningless.

enum FoundationFixtureError: Error { case invalidDate }

func springDayFixture() throws -> TimeInterval {
    guard let zone = TimeZone(identifier: "America/New_York") else {
        throw FoundationFixtureError.invalidDate
    }
    var calendar = Calendar(identifier: .gregorian)
    calendar.timeZone = zone
    guard let start = calendar.date(from: DateComponents(
        year: 2024, month: 3, day: 9, hour: 12
    )), let tomorrow = calendar.date(
        byAdding: .day, value: 1, to: start
    ) else {
        throw FoundationFixtureError.invalidDate
    }
    let fields = calendar.dateComponents(
        [.year, .month, .day, .hour], from: tomorrow
    )
    precondition(fields.day == 10 && fields.hour == 12)
    return tomorrow.timeIntervalSince(start)
}

The expected interval for this named transition is 82,800 seconds. The code first verifies civil meaning, then measures elapsed time. A fixed 86,400-second addition would answer a different question. For the gap/repeat fixtures, write the expected adjustment or skip policy before running Calendar; do not choose policy by accepting whichever result arrives.

The worked text row observes one Character for the decomposed accent and more UTF-8 bytes than its composed counterpart, while equality is true. The emoji-adjacent selection round-trips through NSRange because the conversion uses the exact text. An out-of-bounds range must reject. A partial grapheme range may convert, so use isCharacterAligned to reject it for character-based editing instead of assuming the conversion performs that validation. Do not log real user text to diagnose it.

The number row declares a visible locale and exact decimal or minor-unit contract. The file row treats missing content as empty only if that is the stated store contract, preserves corruption, and reports write failure without replacing it with success. Device rows request protection attributes, locked-open versus locked-reopen observations, and backup policy evidence. No file is created or learner exercise marked complete by this worked answer.

lessons.title: Core Data, SwiftData, contexts, and migration boundaries
lessons.summary: Keep database objects with the context that owns them. Pass snapshots across tasks, define when a save is durable, and test upgrades with actual old store files.
objectives: Explain the model, context, store coordinator or container, store, object ID, and delayed loading.
Run managed-object work through the context and return immutable snapshots.

Compare the checkout’s Core Data stack with SwiftData alternatives and identify the sync work still outside this lesson.

sections.title: A saved record can still be a live owned object
sections.html:
A managed object is a live record tied to a Core Data context. The context tracks identity, changes, relationships, and delayed loading. Reading a property may load persisted values. In Room, a DAO result often becomes an ordinary data value. Do not assume a managed object behaves like that detached Kotlin data class. Passing it to another task hides both its owner and possible I/O. First learn the model, context, and store roles, then choose a snapshot boundary.

The managed object model describes entities, attributes, and relationships. A context is a working set and unit of change. A persistent store coordinator connects contexts to stores in a traditional stack. NSPersistentContainer packages common stack setup without changing those rules. A SQLite store is one backend; Core Data is an object-graph management framework, not just a lightweight SQL wrapper. Raw SQL against its private schema is not a supported general mutation strategy.

The active checkout uses a custom CoreDataStore with NSManagedObjectModel, NSPersistentStoreCoordinator, and a main-queue context. It does not construct NSPersistentContainer in that implementation. Teach the modern convenience container as an alternative, while tracing this stack as it exists. The bundle lookup for the compiled model also matters: a source model present in the repository is not sufficient if the owning target omits the compiled resource.

Choose the store by ownership and durability before comparing frameworks. A server cache that can be reconstructed, an unsent draft, a locally authored history, and a credential need different recovery promises. Sessions 019–020 introduced those distinctions; here they constrain transactions, schema upgrades, and account cleanup.

sections.title: Use the context’s queue even from an actor
sections.html:
Confinement means live context work must use the context’s own queue. A main-queue context belongs on the main queue. Enter a private-queue context through perform or performAndWait. A Swift actor isolates its own state; it is not a dedicated thread and does not make the context belong to that actor’s executor. A detached task is not a shortcut around Core Data’s rule. Keep both language isolation and framework confinement explicit, and pass copied values across the boundary.

Async context perform APIs are available on appropriately recent platforms, including iOS 15+. This example requires Core Data plus a scratch model with SyntheticCard, String id/title/accountID fields. It is not a standalone database just because the declarations compile:

import CoreData
import Foundation

struct PersistentCardSnapshot: Sendable, Equatable {
    let id: String
    let title: String
}
enum CardStoreReadError: Error { case malformed }

func readSyntheticCards(
    in context: NSManagedObjectContext,
    accountID: String
) async throws -> [PersistentCardSnapshot] {
    try await context.perform {
        let request = NSFetchRequest<NSManagedObject>(
            entityName: "SyntheticCard"
        )
        request.predicate = NSPredicate(
            format: "accountID == %@", accountID
        )
        request.sortDescriptors = [
            NSSortDescriptor(key: "id", ascending: true)
        ]
        request.fetchLimit = 100
        return try context.fetch(request).map { object in
            guard let id = object.value(forKey: "id") as? String,
                  let title = object.value(forKey: "title") as? String else {
                throw CardStoreReadError.malformed
            }
            return PersistentCardSnapshot(id: id, title: title)
        }
    }
}

The generic fetch request names the result type. The predicate substitutes a value instead of interpolating untrusted text into predicate syntax. Every fetch and managed-property read occurs in perform. Only Sendable snapshots leave the closure. KVC keys are dynamic model names, so misspellings can be runtime failures; a generated subclass can improve typing. The limit is a safety bound, not a complete pagination design.

sections.title: Distinguish changing, saving, and merging
sections.html:
A save sends tracked changes from a context toward its parent or persistent store. Editing a managed object changes that context first. A child-context save may only update a parent, which still needs to save before data reaches disk. State which save establishes your durable success promise. A title visible in memory does not make an unsent draft durable. Merging is another operation: other contexts may still hold older values until their chosen merge or refresh path runs.

Two contexts can have separate views of the same store state. A background save does not imply every already-loaded UI object instantly reflects it. Configure an appropriate merge path, such as container view-context merging where applicable, or handle save notifications and refresh policy deliberately. Choose a merge policy from the conflict semantics. Store-trump and object-trump strategies can discard different updates; neither is universally safe for user-authored fields.

Pass NSManagedObjectID when a destination context should refetch a reference to the same persisted object. An inserted object may initially have a temporary ID; obtain a permanent identity and ensure required saves are visible before another context resolves it. Even a permanent ID is not authorization or proof the object still exists. Use existingObject(with:) and handle deletion or unavailable-store failure.

Do not keep a live object after resetting its context or unloading its store and assume later access remains valid. For module contracts, snapshots and domain IDs usually make lifetime clearer than leaking object IDs or context instances into presentation. A URI representation of an object ID also remains store-specific, not a universal service identifier.

sections.title: Watch when a property read loads more data
sections.html:
A fault is a managed representation that can load persisted values later. It can reduce initial work, but following relationships may trigger repeated fetches. If a list renders a hundred cards and each reads a separate relationship, it can resemble a network N-plus-one problem: one initial fetch followed by many more. Check what materializes, and measure the actual access pattern before deciding to prefetch everything. Batches, stable sorting, and bounded queries solve different parts of that problem.

Use bounded fetches, stable sorting, appropriate predicates and indexes, and relationship prefetching when measurements show the access pattern benefits. fetchBatchSize affects materialization behavior; it is not a user-visible page token. Offset pagination can drift under concurrent inserts. Choose stable cursor or snapshot semantics when product continuity requires them, and verify the supported store behavior.

Batch updates and deletes can bypass normal managed-object change tracking. Their results may need explicit reconciliation into contexts. A UI holding deleted objects can otherwise show stale state or fail on later access. Store-level efficiency is not permission to skip account predicates, validation, or merge handling. Model callbacks and ordinary object lifecycle work can differ from a batch operation.

The checkout's context is on the main queue. That proves its confinement choice, not that every workload is small enough for smooth rendering. A proposal to move imports should identify the existing call sites, prepare immutable DTOs outside the UI, perform context work on an appropriate queue, and measure on a representative device. This course performs no database benchmark or Instruments capture.

sections.title: Treat a model version as a data promise
sections.html:
Migration moves an old stored model into a newer compatible model. Core Data checks stored metadata when opening a file. Version the model and retain the source versions needed by installed stores. Lightweight migration infers supported changes, including some additions, defaults, and renames with the right identifiers. It cannot infer every type or relationship change, or every change in meaning. A successful open is only the start: check counts, relationships, and actual values from old records.

For changes needing explicit transformation, investigate mapping models, custom migration, or staged migration on supported OS versions. A field rename without its migration identity can become a delete-and-add from the framework's perspective. A non-optional field added to old records needs valid historical values. Even when migration opens successfully, assert record counts, relationships, uniqueness, and actual domain meaning; “no error” is weaker evidence than preservation.

CoreDataStore enables automatic migration and inferred mapping. One failure branch allows a caller-controlled serious-business flag to remove the SQLite file and retry. Record that as the observed recovery policy. It does not prove the data is disposable or that the policy suits a new feature. Read the callers and classify what is stored before considering deletion. A cache rebuild and loss of an irreplaceable draft have very different meanings. Use only synthetic old stores in the exercise.

A migration failure must not silently become a fresh empty collection when local data is irreplaceable. Keep repair, recoverable cache rebuild, user-visible error, and backup/restore separate. Release rollback must also consider whether an older binary can read the upgraded store; reinstalling older source code is not necessarily a data-compatible recovery.

sections.title: SwiftData keeps context and ownership rules
sections.html:
SwiftData is a persistence framework available from iOS 17. Its @Model macro generates persistence behavior from declarations; the resulting model is not a detached Codable value struct. ModelContainer owns schema and storage setup. ModelContext tracks changes. SwiftUI can provide a model context through the environment as a UI owner. That convenience does not allow a live model to cross unrelated tasks. Check newer symbols separately, and define saving, migrations, and snapshot boundaries explicitly.

@ModelActor can supply a model executor and context for serialized model access. Return immutable Sendable values across actor boundaries and resolve identifiers inside the destination owner. A model actor does not make every model magically Sendable. Creating a plain actor around a context without understanding its executor and initialization is not an equivalent isolation strategy.

Use explicit save and failure handling when the workflow needs a durable acknowledgment. Autosave behavior should not define the product's only durability promise. VersionedSchema and SchemaMigrationPlan make schema evolution explicit; lightweight and custom stages still need upgrade fixtures. Recent SDK examples can contain APIs unavailable at the repository's deployment floor, so verify each symbol rather than assuming all SwiftData features started in iOS 17.

No direct SwiftData import or ModelActor declaration was found in the inspected active Projects sources. The existing persistence path is Core Data, alongside other file-backed stores. SwiftData here is a taught alternative, not a completed repository migration. CloudKit-backed synchronization, multi-device conflicts, and framework coexistence deserve separate specialist exercises with real schema and device evidence.

sections.title: Check account ownership where the write occurs
sections.html:
Account scope is the rule connecting a record or operation to its account. A predicate protects a query only if every relevant query and mutation applies that scope. Separate stores per account can clarify cleanup but add opening and migration work. A shared store needs scoped records and clear uniqueness keys. Choose a contract and test it. Disk scoping alone cannot protect a global cached object that still belongs to A when the UI switches to B.

The commit owner is the place that actually validates and changes stored state. Capture account ownership before remote work, then check it there. An actor can check an epoch and await context.perform, but an account reset may happen before that queued closure writes. Put reset ordering and validation inside the serialized command owner that controls mutation, or use a transaction queue with a defined order. An earlier guard on a different owner cannot protect that later persistence operation by itself.

On logout, stop or invalidate old work, clear presentation snapshots, clean the correct account's durable state, and invalidate shared widget/cache representations when required. A file purge, Core Data reset, and Keychain delete are separate operations with different failures. An unavailable store while locked is not the same as a missing account. Preserve enough state to recover without restoring old data under a new session.

Use distinct synthetic accounts and deliberately late operations in the lab. Include failed cleanup and A-to-B-to-A, not only the happy path. Account-scoped persistence is a correctness and privacy boundary, so acceptance must inspect data after ordering changes rather than merely checking that logout returned.

sections.title: Open a real old file to test an upgrade
sections.html:
An upgrade fixture is a synthetic store created with an actual older model. An in-memory store can check predicates, relationships, and many transformations. It cannot establish SQLite migration compatibility, locked-file access, or packaged model resources. Create old-version SQLite files in isolated locations. Open each through the proposed upgrade and check preservation. Record model version, assumptions, OS, and expected records. Keep current-model tests and actual old-file upgrades as separate evidence so their limits stay clear.

For concurrency, assert that no managed object crosses a boundary, changes merge as intended, and stale account commands fail before mutation. Use controlled gates to queue logout before a pending commit. Concurrency debugging diagnostics can expose misuse, but a clean run does not mathematically prove every interleaving safe. A bounded ownership design plus adversarial ordering tests provides stronger evidence.

The existing Core Data stack and file stores make this a mixed persistence checkout. Do not migrate a file store into Core Data just to standardize API names. Write a decision note about query needs, durability, migration cost, data sensitivity, and extension consumers. The smallest reliable store can be appropriate when its writer and schema policies are explicit.

This lesson teaches context and migration fundamentals with a concrete review. Production store repair, CloudKit sync, advanced conflict resolution, and performance tuning of large histories remain specialist practice. No client schema, labels, database, or account data is changed.

The scratch upgrade row needs an actual file, not a reconstructed current-model object: create a V1 SQLite store using the V1 model, save synthetic account A/B records, close the store, then open that same file under V2 with the proposed mapping/inference settings. Assert renamed title values, required defaults, account-scoped counts, relationships, and unchanged durable data after an intentionally rejected upgrade. Keep each fixture in its own temporary directory. Never borrow the client database or delete a failed fixture as a recovery shortcut. Until executed, this is an upgrade procedure; the native persistence workshop supplies the scratch construction boundary.

options: Saving its parent context through the intended store path.
Converting objects to String.
Nothing; all saves always flush every ancestor.
quiz.explanation: A child save can push changes into its parent rather than directly to disk. The stack and success contract determine which saves are required.

quiz.question: Automatic migration is enabled. Does it prove a newly renamed field preserves meaning?
options: Yes, any name change is inferred perfectly.

Only if the database is in Documents.
quiz.explanation: Inference supports particular transformations. A rename needs appropriate identity, and opening successfully is not proof that records and domain values survived.

exercise.brief: Design a synthetic account-scoped card cache with copied UI values and an old-version upgrade fixture. Use the real checkout only for reading.
steps: Describe SyntheticCard and identify which fields are replaceable cache data and which would be irreplaceable.
Use readSyntheticCards and return immutable snapshots rather than live managed objects.
Define background writes, UI merging, permanent IDs, and deleted-record handling.
Hold a delayed write, order account invalidation first, and show that the old command is rejected.
Plan a field rename and a required-field addition using an old store file. Inspect the current recovery branch without running it on client data.
acceptance: All live managed-object access stays within the context owner.
Query and mutation account scope are explicit.
The final mutation validates ownership in its transaction domain.
Upgrade checks assert field values, relationships, and counts, not just successful open.
The submission labels SQLite/device upgrade checks pending until actually executed.
exercise.solution:
The worked model has id, accountID, and title. Its identity uses account plus ID, so A and B can each have a card called alpha. Prepare immutable response values before entering the private context. A transaction command carries the account epoch. Its owner orders resets and writes, validates the epoch, replaces only that account’s records, and saves without admitting a reset between validation and mutation. The UI reads copied values through its own context and follows an explicit merge policy.

The example query in the section demonstrates a typed snapshot boundary. For a generated subclass, replace KVC with typed properties while retaining the same perform ownership. A write failure must throw and leave the old snapshot visible as stale if that is the cache contract. Do not use a catch-all empty array to represent missing, corrupt, unauthorized, and unavailable data.

V1 title renamed to V2 displayTitleMigration identity preserves the synthetic title

Build a real old-model SQLite fixture for the upgrade rows in a scratch test target. In-memory model tests alone do not cover metadata compatibility. For the checkout review, point to the automatic-mapping options and the conditional remove-and-retry branch, then ask which data and callers permit rebuilding. This answer is a design and worked fixture plan; it does not claim a migration was run or the repository's store contents were classified.
